title: The Young Giant

full_text:
A country peasant had a son no bigger than a thumb, who refused to grow regardless of how much bread he ate. One day, a colossal giant passed through the field, scooped up the tiny lad, and carried him to the mountaintops, nourishing him on wild giant's pine-sap and bear milk.

Within a few years, the little boy had grown into an astonishing titan whose shoulders could shake mountains and who could uproot giant oak trees with a casual tug of his hand. He returned to his father's cottage, but his enormous size terrified his parents, who could not afford to feed such an appetite.

The young giant set out into the wide world to seek employment. He hired himself out to a greedy blacksmith, asking as his only wage: two hearty kicks against the smith's backside when the year was completed. The smith laughed, thinking it a jest, but soon realized his new apprentice could hammer an entire anvil into the ground with one strike.

When the year ended, the terrified blacksmith tried to hide and cheat the giant out of his wage, setting fierce traps and throwing boulders from cliffs. But the young giant brushed off the rocks like grains of dust. He returned to the forge, administered the agreed-upon kick that sent the dishonest smith flying over the village steeple, and strode off into the world, an unstoppable champion of fairness and honest contracts.
moral: Great strength is meant to uphold justice and humble arrogance, not to bully the weak.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Young Giant"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
